review: The print gives stanza 1 three lines (the bracketed question, the summons, and the refrain) and stanzas 2–3 four each, so the payload is 3/4/4. Not padded to a rectangle; the metre script calls it irregular for that reason alone.
1:1 the Arabic opens with a parenthetical question (هَلْ فِيكَ يَرَوْنَ يَسُوع); the payload keeps the parentheses so the printed shape and the rhetorical frame are preserved.

1:2 עֶבֶד שׁוֹמֵעַ — the Arabic كُنْ عَبْدًا يَطُوع is 'be an obedient slave'; the Hebrew uses the biblical idiom of the hearing servant (1 Sam 15:22, שְׁמֹעַ … מִזֶּבַח), avoiding the Modern Hebrew צַיְתָן.

3:2 סֵפֶר גַּם־נִדְפָּס — the Arabic سِفْرٌ كَذَاكَ الْمَطْبُوع is 'a book, likewise printed'; נִדְפָּס is the passive participle of דָּפַס (Ps 45:2 of a swift scribe's pen), so the image of a written page stays biblical.

3:3 הַאִם לַשָּׁמַיִם תּוֹלִיכֵם — the Arabic هَلْ لِلسَّمَا تَقُودُهُمْ is 'do you lead them heavenward?'; the Hebrew keeps the interrogative and the direction, with הָאִם as the biblical question opener.
